archetype.name: Dual-Threat (designed-run finisher)
archetype.definition: A big-armed passer who attacks downfield and doubles as Buffalo's goal-line runner and best escape valve, so his value comes as much from scrambles and short-yardage carries as from the pocket.

report.headline: Top-ranked offense, eight rushing touchdowns, four picks: peak Allen, with familiar risk.
report.take:
Five games in, Allen is running the league's most efficient offense. Buffalo ranks 1st in offensive EPA and 2nd in passing EPA, and Allen's 9.05 yards per attempt is 3rd among 43 qualifiers. This is close to his best seasons. His 2024 EPA per play led the league and his 2020 ranked 4th, and his 0.286 pass EPA per dropback sits in that range. What has changed is shape more than level. He is pushing the ball further downfield (9.24 intended air yards against last year's 7.1 aDOT), and the payoff is big: 0.852 EPA on 24 deep attempts and a 17.2 CPOE on intermediate throws.

The fantasy line, 28.6 PPR a game and 1st at the position, rests on the ground game more than the passing does. He has 8 rushing touchdowns in 5 games and has scored on the ground every week. Six of them came on designed runs that average just 2.5 yards a carry. That is a goal-line and short-yardage role: Buffalo hands him the ball inside the 5 instead of throwing it. It also explains an ugly red-zone passing split (-0.152 EPA, 43.5% completions). The scrambling is the real skill underneath. His 16 scrambles produced 1.357 EPA each and 12 first downs, and that is what turns pressure into gains instead of sacks.

The cost is the one he has always paid. Four interceptions put him 32nd of 43, and three came on deep balls. That matches his career: his interception count ranked in the bottom third of qualifiers in all but one season. Four turnover-worthy fumbles add to it. His low point came against the best defense he has faced, the Chargers (6th in defensive EPA): 26.9% bad throws, two picks and four sacks. Against everyone else he has been between good and overwhelming.

Going forward, the passing efficiency looks real. It fits his 2020, 2022 and 2024 seasons and is backed by tracking data. The rushing touchdown pace is not sustainable at eight per five games, even with a stable goal-line role. The defense matters too: Buffalo ranks 30th in defensive EPA, so he will keep playing in shootouts. Four of five games went over, and that keeps his volume and ceiling high.

strengths.title: Scrambles that punish pressure
strengths.body: His 16 scrambles, 9.6% of dropbacks, have produced 12 first downs and 1.357 EPA apiece. That more than pays for a middling 30% pressure-to-sack rate. Extending plays is who he has been for eight years, so this holds up, though the per-scramble EPA will cool from this level.

strengths.title: Vertical and intermediate efficiency
strengths.body: He has 0.852 EPA on throws of 20+ yards and a 17.2 CPOE at 10-19 yards, which drives a 9.05 yards per attempt that ranks 3rd. The intermediate accuracy is the most repeatable part. The deep EPA on 24 attempts will swing, but his arm makes it a lasting strength.

strengths.title: Built-in goal-line role
strengths.body: Six designed-run touchdowns despite 2.5 yards a carry show that Buffalo uses him as its short-yardage finisher. That role is a scheme choice and should continue, which gives him a weekly touchdown path most quarterbacks don't have.

concerns.title: Interceptions remain the tax
concerns.body: His 2.9% interception rate ranks 34th of 43. Three of the four picks came on deep throws, the price of his aggressiveness. His career shows this is a trait, not a slump: his interception totals ranked 49th or worse in four of the last five seasons. Expect roughly one every other game to continue.

concerns.title: Rushing TD pace will regress
concerns.body: Eight rushing touchdowns in five games is far above any realistic full-season rate, even for a goal-line quarterback. As those turn into handoffs or passes, his fantasy output drops toward the low-to-mid 20s even if the efficiency holds.

concerns.title: Thinning protection and receivers
concerns.body: Right tackle Spencer Brown, an 85%-snap starter, left Week 5 with a back injury and is questionable. DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer both missed that game with shoulder injuries. Allen threw only 19 passes in Week 5 and won with his legs, and that may be the template if the injuries linger.

trend.note: He produced passing EPA of +14.5 and +15 in the first two weeks, fell to -0.4 against the Chargers' top-six defense, then recovered to +4.8 and +8.4. Week 5 was a 121-yard rushing game that made up for light passing volume, so his weekly makeup is shifting even though his floor has stayed high.

nextGame.headline: Generous pass defense, high total, but a pass rush that gets home
nextGame.body:
Las Vegas ranks 21st against the pass and 29th on short throws, and it allows 273.6 passing yards and 2.6 touchdowns a game to quarterbacks, 28th in the league. The game is indoors with a 53.5 total, and Buffalo's defense ranks 30th, so expect a game played at Allen's preferred pace. Two things push back. The Raiders are 6th against the run, which makes his designed runs harder. Their 3rd-ranked hit rate means pressure will arrive, which tests both his ball security and his scrambling.

Availability is the key. If Spencer Brown (questionable, back) misses, Las Vegas's pass rush faces a backup tackle, which raises the chance of sacks and hurried throws. Moore and Palmer both carry Week 6 return estimates, but if either sits, the volume shifts to Shakir, Kincaid and Keon Coleman. That suits this defense, which has been hit hard by secondary receivers. On the other side, interior lineman Tonka Hemingway (52% of snaps) is in the concussion protocol, and his absence would weaken their interior push.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders' pass rush vs. Bills' right side
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas ranks 3rd in hit rate and 10th in sack rate. Allen's 30% pressure-to-sack rate is only middling, and a backup right tackle would raise his sack risk. His scrambling (1.357 EPA per scramble) is how he flips this edge back in his favor.

keyMatchups.title: Secondary targets vs. soft coverage
keyMatchups.body: The Raiders have held opposing WR1s 5.9 PPR under their averages but let WR2s and WR3s score nearly 5 over. Tight ends also draw an above-league share of targets against them. Kincaid (0.542 EPA per target) and Coleman (0.982) fit that opening.

keyMatchups.title: Short-area passing over designed runs
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas is 6th in rush defense EPA but 29th on short passes. The path of least resistance is quick-game passing plus scrambles, not designed carries. They have also allowed explosive runs at the 31st-ranked rate, so his scrambles could break big.

nextGame.watch: Whether Spencer Brown plays right tackle. It decides whether Las Vegas's pass rush is a nuisance or a problem.

restOfSeason.body:
The passing efficiency fits the best seasons of his career and should hold near the top ten in EPA per dropback. Buffalo's 30th-ranked defense should keep his volume steady with plenty of high-scoring games. The rushing touchdowns will slow. He will remain the goal-line option, but something like one every other game is more realistic than one or more every week. Interceptions will stay a cost of his deep game.

Expect a top-tier fantasy quarterback whose weekly totals come down from 28.6 toward the low-to-mid 20s. The weekly spread will be wide: 30-plus games when the deep ball and touchdown runs land, high teens against good defenses.
swingFactors: Spencer Brown's back and right-tackle play
Health of DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer
